experiment.title: Within one window, does a broker's probe calls actually complete, or does a meaningful share fail?
experiment.note: Written, hashed and committed before any row of this record's own window is downloaded or read. Nothing in this record may change afterwards; a later change is a new, dated amendment, published first.

question: A broker that cannot be reached, or that errors out on a meaningful share of calls, cannot be routed to safely without a fallback -- regardless of what it would have billed or which provider it would have served from. Within one 7-day window, what fraction of identical, tiny probe calls to each broker complete successfully (an HTTP 200 response with a usable completion), and does any broker's failure rate cross a bar where a customer relying on that broker alone, with no fallback, would be taking on real, noticeable risk?

calibration.disclosed: Reliability was never this repo's own pre-registered question before -- EXP 015's and its amendment-01's preregistrations only ever report callsFailed/callsAttempted as a side metric of the cost-gap question. Both of their own already-published results.json files report a clean record: openrouter, eurouter and requesty each 0 callsFailed of 112 callsAttempted, in both EXP 015's window (2026-10-28..2026-11-04) and amendment-01's window (2026-11-18..2026-11-25). Separately, EXP 022 (provider-serving-stability)'s own window (2026-11-11..2026-11-18) showed every 'stable' pair's n matching its full attempted count, implying 0 failures there too, though that was never the question EXP 022 asked or scored.
calibration.prediction: Unknown whether this record's own window continues that clean streak or not -- that is the point of measuring a window none of those three already looked at, rather than re-describing a fourth zero. Written down before this window's rows are read: given 3 of the 4 weeks since EXP 015's own window opened already show a perfect record, the most likely single outcome is 'reliable' for every broker again, but this record exists precisely so a less-clean week would be caught and reported, not assumed away.
calibration.excludedFromCounting: None of the three windows named above (EXP 015's, amendment-01's, EXP 022's) is read or re-measured by this record.

window.rationale: The one remaining untouched week between EXP 015's window (ending 2026-11-04) and amendment-01's window (starting 2026-11-18) -- EXP 022 already used the other (2026-11-11..2026-11-18, per that record's own window.rationale, which named this earlier week as available for a future follow-up). Chosen by elimination alone, before any row in it was read: it is the only one of the four weeks in this stretch that no prior record in this repository has downloaded or analysed for any purpose.

capture.mechanism: Unchanged: the same scheduled GitHub Actions workflow EXP 015, its amendment-01, and EXP 022 all use (odin-labs-ai/odin-labs, 'R&D telemetry-truth capture', cron 41 */3 * * *, private repo, GitHub-hosted runner). No new capture code, no new key, no new spend; this record only adds a new analysis of rows the existing cron already produces for a window not yet analysed for this question.
capture.codeSha256Reference: Same files, same hashes as pinned in experiments/telemetry-truth/preregistration.json#/capture/sha256 — not re-pinned here since nothing about the capture code changed for this record.
capture.fieldsUsed: broker, ok, httpStatus, ts — the same per-call rows EXP 015 reads, read for a different field (whether the call succeeded at all) than EXP 015's own question (the cost gap, conditional on success) or EXP 022's (which provider served a successful call).

metric.attempted: A row is 'attempted' for a broker if it is inside [window.from, window.to), has a broker field matching, and has a boolean ok field (this excludes the capture's own _header and _trailer summary rows, neither of which carries an ok field at all).
metric.failed: An attempted row with ok !== true. Its httpStatus (if present and not 200) and any error-shaped text field found on the row are recorded for transparency, but are descriptive only -- not part of the decision rule below.

decision.ruleNote: minCalls matches EXP 022's own choice (far below EXP 015's 50 -- that threshold bounds a statistical confidence interval on a continuous gap; this one only needs enough attempted calls that one or two failures are not noise). The 5% marginal ceiling is this record's own reasoning, not reused from elsewhere: on roughly 56 calls/broker/week, that is 1-2 failed calls -- few enough that a human might not notice without counting, but real; a rate above that is the kind of thing a customer without a fallback would actually hit.

perBroker.notEnoughCalls: callsAttempted below minCalls: reported as 'not enough calls', never classified either way.
perBroker.reliable: failureRate === 0. Every attempted call in-window completed.
perBroker.marginal: 0 < failureRate <= 0.05. At least one failure, but not enough to call the broker unreliable on this window alone.
perBroker.unreliable: failureRate > 0.05. A customer routing to this broker alone, with no fallback, would have noticed real failures this week.

stoppingRule: A single pre-registered 7-day window, not a cadence. Report each broker's classification exactly as computed by the frozen analyse.mjs in this directory, whatever it shows. No additional counted window is triggered by an 'unreliable' or 'marginal' result here; a periodic recheck (the same cadence shape as EXP 015's amendment-01) would be its own, separately pre-registered follow-up, not silently added to this record.
cost: $0 marginal. The capture workflow already runs every 3 hours regardless of this record; this record only adds one analysis pass over already-collected rows. No new broker calls, no new keys, no new spend.

analysis.check: node experiments/broker-call-reliability/analyse.mjs --check exits 0 only if results.json is exactly what the frozen script computes from the committed inputs.

reviewNote: Two adversarial reviews with distinct lenses, same discipline as every other record in this repository (EXP 015, its amendment-01, EXP 020, EXP 022, EXP 023), before this record's PR is called ready.
boxBriefNote: Same mechanical shape as EXP 022 and EXP 023's own records (download a fixed pre-registered window's already-collected artifacts from the existing cron; run a small frozen script; commit; open a PR) -- a candidate template for a future bounded automated task once odin-rnd is a reachable target for one (a separate, already-flagged blocker, not this record's). No internal automation system is named here.
limits: Tiny, uncached, list-priced calls on two models, three brokers, one week. A broker's reliability can vary by model, region, load, or time of day in ways this single window and these two tiny test models cannot speak to.

A revoked or missing key (EXP 015's preregistration already documents this happened once, 2026-10-23) produces fewer rows, not a row with ok:false -- this record's callsAttempted counts only what is actually present in the capture, which is a lower bound on calls the probe script tried to make if a key failure suppressed rows entirely before any response was recorded.
One week is a snapshot, not a trend; this record does not claim a broker's reliability this week predicts its reliability next week.
